title: Synergistic NiFe Redox Coupling on Vanadium Phosphorus Oxide for Enhanced Sono‐Fenton Removal of Persistent Organic Pollutants in Aqueous Media
content:
Dye- and antibiotic-laden wastewater is treated over NiFe/VPO under 40 kHz ultrasound. Metallic Ni0 and the V4+/V5+ couple of the support are proposed to help regenerate surface Fe2+, H2O2 is converted into •OH at a sustained rate. Methylene blue, rhodamine B and tetracycline are removed by 93%, 76% and 70% within 20 min.


ABSTRACT

Textile and pharmaceutical effluents co-contaminated with dyes and antibiotics require rapid, light-independent treatment. Bimetallic NiFe nanoparticles were deposited on sonochemically derived vanadium phosphorus oxide (NiFe/VPO) by PVP-assisted NaBH4 co-reduction and applied to the sono-Fenton oxidation of methylene blue (MB), rhodamine B, and tetracycline. XPS indicated the coexistence of three redox couples (Fe2+/Fe3+, Ni0/Ni2+, and V4+/V5+) at the catalyst surface, and NiFe deposition opened the platelet texture of the support. Under ultrasound at pH 3, NiFe/VPO removed 93% of MB within 20 min, also degraded rhodamine B and tetracycline, and showed a higher activity per iron site than Fe/VPO. Scavenger experiments suggested that hydroxyl radicals are the main oxidizing species; a large part of the organic carbon was mineralized, and common inorganic anions and humic acid affected the removal only slightly. Ultrasound accelerated the reaction by about one order of magnitude and removed the surface-limited, pseudo-second-order behavior of the silent process, indicating a synergistic interaction between ultrasound and the catalyst. An electron-transfer pathway in which Ni0 and V4+ assist the regeneration of Fe2+ is proposed. The catalyst retained most of its activity over four cycles, the loss being associated mainly with iron dissolution, and vanadium leaching was low. Redox-active VPO thus emerges as a promising support for heterogeneous sono-Fenton catalysis.
